LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY — OPERATIVE PLAN
─────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM — emergency case, starved status documented.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg at induction.
• LMWH + TED stockings (DVT prophylaxis).
• Consent obtained (emergency consent if incapacitated): perforation risk, conversion to open, wound infection, right-sided port-sit …(truncated)
• Attempt manual reduction: Trendelenburg + analgesia. Do NOT forcibly reduce if tender — strangulation risk.
• Emergency Theatre: irreducible / strangulated hernia — bowel resection risk, consent accordingly.
• Consent: hernia repair — recurrence (1–2% TAPP), chronic groin pain (5%), mesh infection (< 1%), testicular ischaemia/vas injury (< 1%), haematoma.

EMERGENCY LAPAROSCOPIC INGUINAL HERNIA REPAIR (TAPP) — OPERATIVE PLAN
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM from midnight. Consent signed.
• Antibiotics: Co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV at induction (optional — low infection risk if no mesh contamination).
• LMWH + TED stockings.
• Urinary catheter for bilateral or complex repairs (optional for unila …(truncated)
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS — empirical sepsis cover.
• IV Hartmann's 1L over 4h — ensure adequate hydration.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.
HIGH PROBABILITY: Urgent surgical review for likely appendicectomy. Prepare theatre.

• Signs of bowel ischaemia (peritonism, lactate rising, pneumatosis on CT)
• Closed-loop obstruction on CT

• Strangulating hernia as cause

LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY — OPERATIVE PLAN
─────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM — emergency case, starved status documented.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg at induction.
• LMWH + TED stockings (DVT prophylaxis).
• Consent obtained (emergency consent if incapacitated): perforation risk, conversion to open, wound infection, right-sided port-sit …(truncated)

• Plan laparoscopic cholecystectomy — early (< 72h onset) or interval (≥ 6 weeks).
• Obtain surgical consent — laparoscopic cholecystectomy risks/alternatives.
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.

• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.

• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• MRCP — CBD diameter, stone burden, biliary stricture characterisation.

• HPB surgical review — Whipple / Hartmann's if resectable malignancy.

• CXR — identify cause: consolidation, pneumothorax, effusion, cardiomegaly.
• CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2 and D-dimer positive — exclude pulmonary embolism.
• Urine protein:creatinine ratio — nephrotic syndrome (PCR > 300mg/mmol).
• Dietitian referral — pre-operative nutritional support. Delay elective surgery ≥ 4 weeks if possible.
• Prescribe ONS (Ensure/Fortisip) ×2 — pre-op nutritional optimisation (ERAS).
• If albumin < 25 g/L and surgery urgent: parenteral nutrition pre-operatively with nutrition team support.
• Urine ACR — hypertensive nephropathy screen.

• PSA discussion — document informed consent to proceed with test.
